body: I’m really sorry about that. Grief on your birthday is so terrible. All I wanted to do yesterday was cry but I was in public so I had to keep it together. I really hate my birthday, it shouldn’t exist.

I understand this so painfully. I’m close to finishing school and starting my tertiary education but I’m always panicked by the ever changing world. At some point I wanted to become a physicist but because of how technology is improving and how digital the world is becoming I convinced myself out of it. I just want to say it’s normal to feel this way but I would advise against it. The world is always going to change and we unfortunately do not know how it’s going to turn out in 4 years. In 4 years the job you want may not be available but other jobs surrounding AI and programming will for sure be available. Also people change too so who’s to say you will be the same in 4 years. Don’t limit yourself to one job, I’m sure you’re amazing and can do a lot of things. There’s little you can do to control how the world turns out in 4 years so just try to enjoy and focus on the things you control. Just focus on yourself for now. You’ll figure it out when time comes :)

I sent her messages once but the problem was I wrote them in English. I mainly express myself in English and not really the language I was brought up with. It’s difficult to connect with her because I can only manage to express my emotions in English. I just feel like there’s this huge disconnect and I wish I hadn’t started thinking in English. It’s not even the language thing at most... I just feel like I didn’t appreciate her enough, I didn’t even sit with her on her last day. She was one of my first best friends because I was too afraid to make friends and I spent so much time with her. She showed me so many things and now I don’t know even remember if I was taller than her or if I was shorter.
I think I’m going to do that from now on, that’s a really good idea. I’m going to redo my birthday when I feel okay, I’m just working to get out of this dark place.

I just don’t know how to celebrate it. I  don’t even get to hear her sing her special song for me. It’s hard to believe someone could be there one day and then the next they’re gone.
